newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuraya says to absorb small drug company in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Kuraya says to absorb small drug company in Oct.

text.p: Kuraya Corp, Japan's second largest pharmaceutical wholesaler, said on Tuesday that it would take over a Nagano-based drug company on October 1 in a combined stock and cash merger.
Kuraya said that the decision to merge with Kawai Corp, currently 20-percent owned by Kuraya, was made to strengthen its service facilities to hospitals and drug stores.
The merger ration will be one to 0.7 -- with seven Kuraya stocks, with face value of 50 yen per share, exchanged for one Kawai share, whose face value is 500 yen, the company said in a statement.
The company also said it would pay an additional 25 yen per share to shareholders of Kawai as of September 30 this year.

The merged company would hold assets worth 286.72 billion yen and is expected to post sales of 471.8 billion yen for the year ending in March 1998, and 510.35 billion yen in the following year, Kuraya said.
